newsitem.title: USA: Midwest propane prices near 7-year highs.
newsitem.headline: Midwest propane prices near 7-year highs.

text.p: Propane prices in the Midwest jumped to the highest levels in nearly seven years Wednesday on fears that consumers may run out of the key heating fuel as winter sinks its teeth into the nation's heartland.
But as spot market prices approached $1 per gallon -- triple the levels of a year ago -- some traders said inventory fears had pushed prices to unreasonable heights.
"It seems like there's a lot of hype in the market. Prices seem overvalued," one trader said.

Some experts said the market was waiting for new weekly numbers that could provide a better gauge of supplies, such as a report on weekly inventories due later Wednesday from the Energy Information Administration, a unit of the Department of Energy.

In late afternoon trading, propane for prompt delivery at the Midwest trading hub of Conway, Kansas, was offered at 94 cents a gallon, with some supplies for late-December delivery sold early in the day at 97.25 cents.
Conway prices jumped 15 cents a gallon Tuesday, one day after the American Petroleum Institute said that propane inventories in the Midwest states posted a large drop in October.
The monthly report by the API, an industry group, estimated Midwest inventories in late October shrank by more than 3.5 million barrels from a month earlier -- leaving only 12.5 million in reserve.
Nationwide, propane inventories totalled 49.5 million barrels at the end of October, about six million less than a year ago.
An early Midwest cold snap in November may have further cut into inventories, as did strong demand from farmers for drying a late corn crop.
Some traders speculated that the region's propane inventories may have shrunk another two to four million barrels since late October, leaving current primary stocks at bare-bone levels.

But others said inventories are not low enough to justify current Midwest prices that are triple the 33.00 cents at this time last year, and the highest since the $1.10-per-gallon record reached in 1989.
"Inventories are low, but not inordinately bad," one Midwest trader said, expressing surprise that prices have soared so dramatically even before the beginning of winter.
On the Gulf Coast, spot propane at the trading hub of Mont Belvieu, Texas, hovered at 71.00 cents a gallon after jumping 1.50 cents Tuesday in sympathy with the Conway market's blustering strength.
"That's more than double this time last year," one Gulf Coast trader said.
